headline: High-risk filesystem and shell overlap in Plandex can conflict with Opik’s broad egress, while prompt-injection risk is limited by lack of a documented shared channel.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No documented direct channel exists between Opik and Plandex, but Plandex can read/write project files and Opik can emit REST API outputs that may be manually bridged. That makes prompt injection plausible only through unusual copy/paste or file handoff, not by default. The pairwise pathway is inferred, not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF the operator copies Opik output into a Plandex prompt or file
IF Plandex ingests project files containing Opik-generated instructions
mitigations: Keep Opik outputs out of Plandex prompts
Use a separate review file for model outputs
Strip instruction-like text before handoff
Disable any auto-import of generated text
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between tools

B_data_leakage.rationale: Plandex reads and writes a project directory and sends context to a model provider; Opik has broad network egress. If the shared workspace contains sensitive source code or secrets, Plandex can upload it and Opik can also exfiltrate context via API calls. This is a default-configuration exposure for the pair, though the exact shared data path is only partially documented.
conditions: IF the project directory contains secrets or regulated source code
IF Plandex forwards file contents to its model provider during planning
mitigations: Remove secrets from the shared project directory
Use a scrubbed sandbox copy of the repo
Rotate any exposed API keys
Limit Opik to non-sensitive datasets
requires-engineering: enforce content redaction before model upload

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Plandex has write_filesystem, modify_git_state, and shell execution; Opik has broad network egress and REST API access. In a shared repo or workspace, Plandex can mutate files and git state while Opik can independently send data outward, creating a dangerous overlap with irreversible changes and exfiltration potential. The conflict is directly supported by both profiles.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or workspace
IF Plandex auto-applies changes while Opik is active
mitigations: Run the agents on separate copies of the workspace
Disable auto-apply in Plandex
Pause Opik during git-mutating steps
Use a manual approval gate before commits
requires-engineering: add file-locking around shared paths

D_cascading_error.rationale: Plandex uses a review-then-apply workflow, but it can still act on model-generated plans, and Opik can produce outputs that may be treated as authoritative by an operator or downstream tool. The pairwise risk is that Opik’s output becomes Plandex input without verification, causing incorrect edits or actions. The sandbox reduces but does not eliminate the cascade.
conditions: IF Opik output is pasted into Plandex as instructions or plan text
IF Plandex auto-apply is enabled or the review step is skipped
mitigations: Require human review of Opik outputs before use
Keep Plandex in review-then-apply mode
Disable auto-apply
Cross-check generated plans against source files
requires-engineering: add structured validation between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and do not declare regulated-data certifications or residency constraints, so no specific residency breach is evidenced. The only concrete compliance concern is that Plandex handles model provider API keys and source code, while Opik has broad egress; this creates a small but real policy-mismatch risk if sensitive code is processed. The other agent is cited because the risk is pairwise.
conditions: IF regulated source code or secrets are placed in the shared workspace
IF organizational policy forbids sending that data to external model providers
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the workspace
Use a self-hosted model backend where possible
Review retention settings for both tools
Separate sensitive and non-sensitive projects
requires-engineering: document a data-handling policy for the pair
